brief.headline: Push for ₹1.87/NOS on PET bottles (16.6% below today) and ask for 45-day terms to free up ₹93078 cash

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹1.87/NOS for the PET amber bottle, matching what Suraj Blow Plast charges us today
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.87/NOS to Suraj; TPAC at ₹2.18/NOS is 16.6% higher for the same bottle. Market research shows 28 mm caps typically trade at ₹0.85–0.95/pc with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so rigid plastic pricing has room to move.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 45 days after receipt

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is financially stable — they carry an [ICRA] A / Stable rating and they keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell. But their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as similar firms at 79d), they pay suppliers in 17d (much faster than peers at 33d), and they borrow money at about 10.27%. That means early payment is worth roughly 10% to them. The bad news: we're tiny — ₹11.32 L is just 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, so they won't bend on price for us alone. The plan: use Suraj's ₹1.87 price as proof TPAC is high, dangle faster payment for a price cut, and line up Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr rigid-packaging giant) as a second source to show we can walk.

evidence.point: TPAC charges us ₹2.18/NOS for the PET amber bottle; Suraj charges ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% gap
Closing that gap saves us ₹28644 a year
We're 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — tiny leverage on our own
They borrow at 10.27%, so paying them 15 days faster (worth ₹46539 to us) costs them about 0.4% — a fair swap for a price cut
Credit rating [ICRA] A / Stable and they keep ₹4 per ₹100 sold (3.8% margin) — healthy, not desperate
Their cash is stuck for 79 days (peers also 79d) but they pay suppliers in 17d vs peer 33d — cash is slightly tight

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr — makes pharma bottles, caps, preforms; proven second-source candidate with strong health (B 65/100)

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr, B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging; robust alternate for bottles and closures

risks: We're only ₹11.32 L to them (0.02% of revenue) — they may ignore us unless we bundle more volume or commit multi-year
GST filing delays and EPF payment delays flagged — watch for any supply hiccups; ask for on-time delivery guarantees
Their financial score is 4/10 and Altman Z is 2.77 (grey zone) — not distressed but not rock-solid; don't squeeze so hard you destabilise a small supplier
Suraj at ₹1.87 is our only proof TPAC is high — if Suraj can't scale or qualify a second item, we lose the benchmark; start qualifying Manjushree now
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to match the ₹1.87 price Suraj gives us on the same PET bottle and move to 45-day terms — in return we'll commit volume and pay you faster than your typical customer.
